correctness.rationale: The exact zero-sum quadratic form decomposes into strictly negative peripheral fluctuation terms, a completed square and a two-by-two Schur complement. Its smaller eigenvalue equals gamma-beta-sqrt(delta^2+z^2). The scalar crossing is unique on (1,2] by a proved exponential sign/derivative argument; all p>2 fail by a negative principal diagonal. At the crossing the kernel has the claimed dimension, and the rank and asymptotic/size laws follow. The critical algebraic reduction was reproduced exactly on 525 rational cases; 100 separate Gram inertia cases and 81 monotonic comparisons corroborate the analytical proof.

value.rationale: The graph family is a classical two-clique bridge structure already treated in the spectral literature. The evaluated exact negative-type exponent for every pair of clique orders is a natural unknown metric invariant, with a sharp critical Hilbert dimension, strict monotonicity under clique growth, and an explicit universal asymptotic with size correction. This is not a numerical special-case census or a rewrite of ordinary distance inertia.
